newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI BOOSTED BY ASSET SWAP, SALE OF STAKE.
newsitem.headline: JCI BOOSTED BY ASSET SWAP, SALE OF STAKE.

text.p: JCI Ltd shares bounced in early trade on Wednesday boosted by a two million share asset swap and the sale of its stake in Consolidated Murchison to Metorex Pty Ltd for an undisclosed sum.
"The asset swap could have created a bit of interest. There is a rumour that the (Consmurch) deal was done at 450 cents which is good for them," a dealer said.
The share jumped 200 cents, or 6.2 percent, to 34.25 rand in a volume of 2.05 million shares valued at 66 million rand. Consmurch was last unchanged at 440 cents.
But dealers said JCI shares were overvalued at these levels and fundamentals for the mining sector were still bearish.
"I think it (the sale) has helped them but not in the long term. The fundamentals are still the same. We still think the share is too high. We do not like it," another dealer said.
"It is hard to turn around the mines. I do not see how they would be able to do that," one added.
JCI said it had supported Consmurch, the world's largest producer of antimony, with 10.4 million rand's worth of loan finance but it was viewed as a poor fit, primarily due to its size.

Consmurch mines in the Letaba district of South Africa for antimony ore, from which it produced 9,413 tonnes of antimony concentrates in the year to June 30, 1996. Gold and silver are recovered as by-products.
